children.translated_text: That <s>Bhavānī</s>, O <s>Bhavānī</s> —
skilled in the destruction of afflictions,
resplendent like autumn, like an autumn cloud,
seated on a white lion-throne — salutations!
May the first rays of your sky-jewel [the sun],
those that partake of the redness of rising, bestow auspiciousness —
those which, at the great festivals of the birth of day,
make the ladies of the directions appear as if their faces are reddened with <s>sindūra</s> (vermillion)
Bound by the passion of offering, preceded by vigorous churning —

children.text: arthān kathaṃ jhaṭiti tān prakṛtān na dadyuḥ
children.translated_text: how could they not quickly yield those natural meanings?
Like exceedingly gentle thieves, the words of great poets
forcibly distribute even secondary meanings

children.text: arthān kathaṃ jhaṭiti tān prakṛtān na dadyuḥ

children.translated_text: Glass is a gem, a gem is glass —
for those [who think so], they are indeed other beings;
but there are those of good intellect for whom
glass is glass and a gem is a gem
Indeed, O <s>kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison), this is the course of your abode,
taught by one who indicated ever-higher and more distinguished positions —
first in the heart of the ocean, then in [the throat of] the Bull-marked one [<s>Śiva</s>],
and now you dwell in the speech of wicked people
Wealth in adversity, an ornament at a festival,
a refuge in fear for one's life, a lamp at night —
capable of bearing the weight of manifold services,
who is there like you, a true gem?
<s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), like an unchained wanton woman of the wicked,
through paths thick with the grime of darkness,
is unable to endure even the mere sound
that arises from the ornament of the virtuous

children.text: māne necchati vārayaty upaśame kṣmām ālikhantyāṃ hriyāṃ
children.translated_text: When pride refuses, when restraint forbids, when modesty scratches the ground,

children.text: svātantrye parivṛtya tiṣṭhati karau vyādhūya dhairyaṃ gate
children.translated_text: when independence turns its back, when courage departs shaking its hands —

children.text: tṛṣṇe tvām anubadhnatā phalam iyatprāptaṃ janenāmunā
children.translated_text: O Desire, this much fruit has been obtained by this person who follows you:

children.text: yaḥ spṛṣṭo na padā sa eva caraṇau spraṣṭuṃ na saṃmanyate
children.translated_text: he whom he never touched with his foot, that very one does not deign to touch his feet

children.text: māne necchati vārayaty upaśame kṣmām ālikhantyāṃ hriyāṃ
svātantrye parivṛtya tiṣṭhati karau vyādhūya dhairyaṃ gate
tṛṣṇe tvām anubadhnatā phalam iyatprāptaṃ janenāmunā
yaḥ spṛṣṭo na padā sa eva caraṇau spraṣṭuṃ na saṃmanyate

children.translated_text: Let it fall into water, let it go to another direction,
let it enter fire, or let it go to the earth —
this sun — what diminution is there in its qualities,
which cause wonder in the entire world?
Those of good conduct who discriminate between right and wrong meaning —
see how they describe this one [the sun];
what thieves, unchaste women, and the like say about it —

children.text: tad gṛhyate yadi kṛtaṃ tad ahaskareṇa
children.translated_text: if that is accepted, then [blame] what the sun has done

children.text: tad gṛhyate yadi kṛtaṃ tad ahaskareṇa
pātaḥ pūṣṇo bhavati mahate nopatāpāya yasmāt
children.translated_text: The setting of <s>Pūṣan</s> (the Sun) does not cause great distress, for

children.text: kāle prāpte ka iha na yayur yānti yāsyanti vāstam*
children.translated_text: who in this world has not gone, does not go, or will not go to rest when the time comes?
But this is what pains exceedingly: that in that very vast sky
an opportunity has been found by those darknesses that are outside the world

children.text: pātaḥ pūṣṇo bhavati mahate nopatāpāya yasmāt
kāle prāpte ka iha na yayur yānti yāsyanti vāstam*

children.translated_text: Let those counted in the reverse order enter the row;
the earlier ones might thereby feel at least some shame —

children.text: santo 'py asanta iva cet pratibhānti bhānor
children.translated_text: even the worthy appear as if unworthy; the foremost among the cool-rayed ones [stars]
in a sky enveloped by the radiance of the sun

children.text: santo 'py asanta iva cet pratibhānti bhānor

children.translated_text: When that sun has set, the moon will remove the pain

children.text: vyathāṃ candro neṣyaty anucitam ato nāsty asadṛśam
children.translated_text: of separation from the blossoming of the three worlds — there is nothing unfitting in this;

children.text: idaṃ cetastāpaṃ janayatitarām atra yad amī
children.translated_text: but what produces heartache all the more here is that these
lamps have arisen, their flames bound to the task of destroying darkness

children.text: vyathāṃ candro neṣyaty anucitam ato nāsty asadṛśam
idaṃ cetastāpaṃ janayatitarām atra yad amī

children.translated_text: Apart from the sun, whatever has been accomplished by the moon also
that does not touch real substance;
the name '<s>khadyota</s>' (firefly) for a mere insect
[was given] by someone who was easily pleased
O insect-jewel, now during the day
when your lovely white rays are hidden by the rays of the sun,
covered with the grime of dense darkness —

children.text: daśadiśi niśi yad virājasi tad anyat
children.translated_text: that you shine in the ten directions at night is another matter

children.text: daśadiśi niśi yad virājasi tad anyat

children.translated_text: Whether it flickers within beings or is a trifling superimposition of qualities —

children.text: tasmai kātaramohanāya mahaso leśāya mā svasti bhūt
children.translated_text: may there be no well-being for that fragment of light that deludes the timid!
For by this insect named 'firefly,' whose flashing shadow is reddish,
we are mocked with the false impression of a moving jewel

children.text: tasmai kātaramohanāya mahaso leśāya mā svasti bhūt

children.translated_text: Only the elephant, struck on its lofty mountain-[like forehead] by the continuous blows
of the tip of the tusk-spear, truly knows
the pain of the blow from the cage of the lion's paw —
not the jackal, a mere puppy of a dog, rendered motionless by a single growl
O <s>cātaka</s> (rain-bird) chick, addicted to lofty heights,
now make your entreaty to your own head;
if this one [the cloud] desires it, in the extended directions

children.text: tāḥ svacchaśītamadhurāḥ kva nu nāma nāpaḥ
children.translated_text: where indeed are there no waters — clear, cool, and sweet?

children.text: asya etad icchati yadi pratatāsu dikṣu
tāḥ svaccha-śīta-madhurāḥ kva nu nāma nā apaḥ

children.translated_text: That unprecedented reversal of the tongue's [taste], that fickleness of the ears,

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ sā madavismṛtasvaparadik kiṃ bhūyasoktena vā
children.translated_text: that gaze forgetful in intoxication of its own and others' space — what more need be said?

children.text: itthaṃ niścitavān asi bhramara he yad vāraṇo 'dyāpy asā*
children.translated_text: O bee, you have concluded thus — that this elephant even today

children.text: antaḥśūnyakaro niṣeyata iti bhrātaḥ ka eṣa grahaḥ
children.translated_text: sits with an empty interior of the hand — O brother, what is this delusion?

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ sā mada-vismṛta-sva-para-dik kiṃ bhūyasa ūktena vā
itthaṃ niścitavān asi bhramara he yad vāraṇo 'dya apy asā*
antaḥ-śūnya-karo niṣeyata iti bhrātaḥ ka eṣa grahaḥ

children.translated_text: That cleverness of yours in discerning the true nature of appropriate milk-water,

children.text: saṃlāpās te sa ca mṛdupadanyāsahṛdyo vilāsaḥ
children.translated_text: those conversations, and that charming gait with soft steps —

children.text: āstāṃ tāvad baka yadi tathā vetthi kiṃ cic chlathāṃsas
children.translated_text: let all that be, O crane; if you know even this much — how, with relaxed shoulders,

children.text: tūṣṇīm evāsitum api sakhe tvaṃ kathaṃ me na haṃsaḥ
children.translated_text: to sit in silence — O friend, how are you not my swan?

children.text: saṃlāpās te sa ca mṛdu-pada-nyāsa-hṛdyo vilāsaḥ
āstāṃ tāvad baka yadi tathā vetthi kiṃ cic chlatha-aṃsas
tūṣṇīm evā asitum api sakhe tvaṃ kathaṃ me na haṃsaḥ

children.translated_text: Seeing a pot of fresh curd fallen on the road in an empty [place],
unguarded, swelling with pride, with neck raised high —
if the one-eyed crow, agitated with a hundred impulses,

children.text: yadi na kurute kākaḥ kāṇaḥ kadā nu kariṣyati
children.translated_text: does not perform those those characteristic antics of its own, when will it ever?

children.text: yadi na kurute kākaḥ kāṇaḥ kadā nu kariṣyati
nṛtyantaḥ śikhino manoharam amī śrāvyaṃ paṭhantaḥ śukā
children.translated_text: Peacocks dance charmingly, parrots recite melodiously —

children.text: vīkṣyante na ta eva khalv iha ruṣā vāryanta evāthavā
children.translated_text: are they not seen here, or are they rather driven away in anger?
By this powerful sorcerer [the crow] who gained credibility by telling

children.text: sampraty etad anargalaṃ balibhujā māyāvinā bhujyate
children.translated_text: travelers' wives of the arrival of their beloved — now this [food] is enjoyed without restraint

children.text: nṛtyantaḥ śikhino manoharam amī śrāvyaṃ paṭhantaḥ śukā
vīkṣyante na ta eva khalv iha ruṣā vāryanta evāthavā
sampraty etad anargalaṃ balibhujā māyāvinā bhujyate
karabha rasabhāt kroṣṭuṃ vāñcchasy aho śravaṇajvaraḥ
children.translated_text: O young camel, you wish to cry out more than a donkey — ah, what a torment to the ears!
Or perhaps your long, crooked neck is your refuge;
weary from the turning of your wide throat, the voice that will emerge will be long —

children.text: diyati, samaye ko jānīte bhaviṣyati kasya kim
children.translated_text: it flows forth; who knows what will happen to whom at the [appointed] time?

children.text: karabha rasabhāt kroṣṭuṃ vāñcchasy aho śravaṇajvaraḥ
diyati, samaye ko jānīte bhaviṣyati kasya kim

children.translated_text: Many are the inner hollows,
and many thorns are on the outside —
how could the qualities of the lotus stalk
not be fragile?
O lotus, why do you have the cause for concealment
in your many long white virtues?

children.text: asty eva tān paśyati ced anāryā
children.translated_text: If the ignoble one [<s>Lakṣmī</s>/Fortune] sees them, indeed
she does not place her foot [there], as if frightened

children.text: asty eva tān paśyati ced anāryā

children.translated_text: Not born from mud, not addicted to dwelling in water,
your body anointed with a luster that steals the jewel-radiance of the land-lotus —

children.text: vyadhāsyad durvedhā hṛdayalaghimānaṃ yadi na te
children.translated_text: if the perverse creator had not made you light-hearted,

children.text: tvam evaiko lakṣmyāḥ paramam abhaviṣyaḥ padam iha
children.translated_text: you alone would have been the supreme abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s> (Fortune) in this world

children.text: vyadhāsyad durvedhā hṛdayalaghimānaṃ yadi na te
tvam evaiko lakṣmyāḥ paramam abhaviṣyaḥ padam iha

children.translated_text: Let the cricket chirp loudly for long
having climbed a tree on the road —
in the quality of sound that pervades the directions,
the conch is the ground for esteem
The conch is a mere bone-remnant, cracked, or dead;
truly, it is blown with another's breath;

children.text: kiṃ tūccaraty eva hi so 'sya śabdaḥ
children.translated_text: but indeed that sound of its does issue forth —

children.text: śrāvyo na yo yo na sadarthaśaṃsī
children.translated_text: which is not pleasant, which does not proclaim true meaning

children.text: kiṃ tūccaraty eva hi so 'sya śabdaḥ
śrāvyo na yo yo na sadarthaśaṃsī

children.translated_text: Just as your shoots [yield] flowers,
just as your flowers [yield] the abundance of fruits,
just as your fruit-abundance [yields] new growth —
alas, O mother, where have such trees gone?
Indeed, the Creator was rightly laborious
in fashioning this one — not in vain;
what use is a fruit to the sandalwood tree
that is not in accord with its own nature?

children.text: grathitaḥ eṣa mithaḥ kṛtaśṛṅkhalair viṣadharair adhiruhya mahājaḍaḥ /
children.translated_text: Climbing upon this very dense [sandalwood tree], intertwined in chains of venomous serpents — / the sandalwood, unsupported by fragrant flowers, is thereby deprived of fruit //

children.text: malayajaḥ sumanobhir anāśrito yad ata eva phalena viyujyate //
children.translated_text: We tolerate the venomous serpents on the sandalwood —

children.text: grathitaḥ eṣa mithaḥ kṛtaśṛṅkhalair viṣadharair adhiruhya mahājaḍaḥ /
malayajaḥ sumanobhir anāśrito yad ata eva phalena viyujyate //

children.translated_text: a beautiful thing rendered unprotectable;
tell me, O <s>khadira</s> (acacia) tree, have you accumulated your thorns
in order to protect your own dignity?
What has not the flower or fruit done, even if somewhat unfitting,
in accordance with proper conduct toward the sandalwood?

children.text: kiṃ candanasya na kṛtaṃ kusumaṃ phalaṃ vā
children.translated_text: We are ashamed as we approach
its vicinity, having taken up large axes
Obtained with difficulty, like <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) — but would it grant immortality?

children.text: kiṃ candanasya na kṛtaṃ kusumaṃ phalaṃ vā
labdhaṃ cirād amṛtavat kim amṛtyave syād
children.translated_text: Would it bestow long life like a rejuvenating elixir?
This is the fruit: that this obstinate, wicked palmyra palm,
scorched by the curse of travelers, bears fruit after a hundred years
That sandalwood tree is cut down — the satisfied friend; you serpents have fled and come [here],

children.text: labdhaṃ cirād amṛtavat kim amṛtyave syād
chinnas tṛptasuhṛt sa candanatarur yūyaṃ palāyyāgatā
children.translated_text: addicted to the pleasure of habitual enjoyment — those [comforts] there are forgotten by you daily;

children.text: bhogābhyāsasukhāsikāḥ pratidinaṃ tā vismṛtās tatra vaḥ
children.translated_text: if no reprisal was made against that cutter with the fire-brand of the poison at your fang-tips,

children.text: daṃṣṭrākoṭiviṣolkayā pratikṛtaṃ tasya prahartur na cet
children.translated_text: why did you not yourselves go, piece by piece, along with him, O enjoyers?

children.text: kiṃ tenaiva saha svayaṃ na lavaśo yātāḥ stha bho bhoginaḥ

children.translated_text: Is it contentment or incapacity or perhaps disregard for that one?

children.text: chinnas tṛptasuhṛt sa candanatarur yūyaṃ palāyyāgatā
bhogābhyāsasukhāsikāḥ pratidinaṃ tā vismṛtās tatra vaḥ
daṃṣṭrākoṭiviṣolkayā pratikṛtaṃ tasya prahartur na cet
kiṃ tenaiva saha svayaṃ na lavaśo yātāḥ stha bho bhoginaḥ
saṃtoṣaḥ kim aśaktatā kim athavā tasminn asambhāvanā
children.translated_text: Is it greed, or is it instability, or is it rather hatred?

children.text: lobho vāyam utānavasthitir iyaṃ pradveṣa evāthavā
children.translated_text: Leave aside [the association] with fitting, fruitful floral beauty, O ill-fated one —

children.text: āstāṃ khalv anurūpayā saphalayā puṣpaśriyā durvidhe
children.translated_text: you have not even made a connection with the sandalwood, however unfitting

children.text: sambandho 'nanurūpayāpi na kṛtaḥ kiṃ candanasya tvayā

children.translated_text: Were you born at a crossroads? Your shade is dense — what [use] is shade?

children.text: saṃtoṣaḥ kim aśaktatā kim athavā tasminn asambhāvanā
lobho vāyam utānavasthitir iyaṃ pradveṣa evāthavā
āstāṃ khalv anurūpayā saphalayā puṣpaśriyā durvidhe
sambandho 'nanurūpayāpi na kṛtaḥ kiṃ candanasya tvayā
kiṃ jāto 'si catuṣpathe ghanatarachāyo 'si kiṃ chāyayā
children.translated_text: You are laden with fruit — what [use] are the burdens of fruit? You are full — what [use] is bowing?

children.text: saṃyuktaphalito 'si kiṃ phalabharaiḥ pūrṇo 'si kiṃ sannataḥ
children.translated_text: O noble tree, endure now, O friend — the pulling of branches and tops,

children.text: he sadvṛkṣa sahasva samprati sakhe śākhāśikhākarṣaṇa
children.translated_text: the agitation, cracking, and breaking by people with their own wicked actions
Well-rooted, of renowned height, of thick and pleasant shade, standing on a good path,

children.text: kiṃ jāto 'si catuṣpathe ghanatarachāyo 'si kiṃ chāyayā
saṃyuktaphalito 'si kiṃ phalabharaiḥ pūrṇo 'si kiṃ sannataḥ
he sadvṛkṣa sahasva samprati sakhe śākhāśikhākarṣaṇa

children.translated_text: frequented by the good — reflecting thus, a traveler took refuge under a palmyra;
a man's power is only this much: it may fruit today, or tomorrow, or

children.text: puṃsaḥ śaktir iyaty asau tu phaled adyāthavā śvo 'thavā
children.translated_text: sometime, or perhaps someday, or perhaps never — but the Creator is the master

children.text: kāle kvāpy athavā kadācid athavā na tv eva vedhāḥ prabhuḥ

children.translated_text: A human lifetime has been spent at your root by this body that is drying up;

children.text: puṃsaḥ śaktir iyaty asau tu phaled adyāthavā śvo 'thavā
kāle kvāpy athavā kadācid athavā na tv eva vedhāḥ prabhuḥ
tvanmūle puruṣāyuṣaṃ gatam idaṃ dehena saṃśuṣyatā
children.translated_text: from this point there is not even the power to live for the smallest moment more;

children.text: kṣodīyaṃsam api kṣaṇaṃ param atah śaktiḥ kutaḥ prāṇitum
children.translated_text: so farewell, grow to great fullness — even now, what is our hurry?

children.text: tat svasty astu vivṛdddhim ehi mahatīm adyāpi kā nas tvarā
children.translated_text: O auspicious one, you have borne fruit, O palmyra palm — in [your] children or grandchildren!

children.text: kalyāṇin! phalitāsi tālaviṭapin! putreṣu pautreṣu vā

children.translated_text: 'Let us see what this one will bring' — with such contempt, long ignored

children.text: tvanmūle puruṣāyuṣaṃ gatam idaṃ dehena saṃśuṣyatā
kṣodīyaṃsam api kṣaṇaṃ param atah śaktiḥ kutaḥ prāṇitum
tat svasty astu vivṛdddhim ehi mahatīm adyāpi kā nas tvarā
kalyāṇin! phalitāsi tālaviṭapin! putreṣu pautreṣu vā
paśyāmaḥ kim ayaṃ prapatsyata iti svalpābhrasiddhakriyair
children.translated_text: by ministers whose accomplishments required but little cloud-work, powerfully incited to action —

children.text: darpād dūram upekṣitena balavat karmeritair mantribhiḥ
children.translated_text: having gained free course and become impossible to guard against, releasing thunderbolts —
alas, such a prosperous hill-village was burned by that mighty storm-cloud enemy!

children.text: sphītas tādṛg aho ghanena ripuṇā dagdho girigrāmakaḥ

children.translated_text: Well done, O host of uprising clouds! Well done! This is to be contemplated on earth by the wise —

children.text: paśyāmaḥ kim ayaṃ prapatsyata iti svalpābhrasiddhakriyair
darpād dūram upekṣitena balavat karmeritair mantribhiḥ
sphītas tādṛg aho ghanena ripuṇā dagdho girigrāmakaḥ
sādhūtpātaghanauga sādhu sudhiyā dhyeyaṃ dharāyām idaṃ
children.translated_text: who else is able to accomplish such a difficult deed? It befits only you —

children.text: ko 'nyaḥ kartum alaṃ tavaiva ghaṭate karmedṛśaṃ duṣkaram
children.translated_text: lightning on whatever few fields are beneficial to all,
rain-showers on all the barren, burnt sand-deserts
When thirst has been obtained by a cow, a deer, a bird, or any other —

children.text: sādhūtpātaghanauga sādhu sudhiyā dhyeyaṃ dharāyām idaṃ
ko 'nyaḥ kartum alaṃ tavaiva ghaṭate karmedṛśaṃ duṣkaram
labdhāyāṃ tṛṣi gomṛgasya vihagasyānyasay vā kasya cid
children.translated_text: that your rain would be a service to them, let that be set far aside;

children.text: vṛṣṭyā syād bhavadīyayopakṛtir ity āstāṃ davīyasy adaḥ
children.translated_text: even to this utterly undeserving wasteland, O cloud —
look, again and again, that same harsh, scorched complexion has appeared

children.text: jātā paśya punaḥ punar eva paruṣā saivāsya dagdhā chaviḥ

children.translated_text: Abandoning other waters suitable for drinking and rinsing

children.text: labdhāyāṃ tṛṣi gomṛgasya vihagasyānyasay vā kasya cid
vṛṣṭyā syād bhavadīyaya ūpakṛtir ity āstāṃ davīyasy adaḥ
jātā paśya punaḥ punar eva paruṣā saivāsya dagdhā chaviḥ

children.translated_text: of this one who wishes to serve you —
O desertless one, are you not ashamed, O cloud, of [offering] waters
fit only for the meanest purposes to the people?
From women to children, this [ocean] is widely known
to be kept away from the thirsty by its very undrinkability;
with its wave upon wave made fearsome by terrible crocodiles with gaping fangs —
does it further frighten with anything else?
Having cried out on all sides with deep, thick roars boasting of your own greatness,
O ocean, why do you torment the cavern of our ears?

children.text: kruśitvā kliśnāsi śrutikuharam abdhe kim iti naḥ
children.translated_text: Here, one single tuft-haired [<s>Agastya</s>] was born from a pot, from whom, with all

children.text: ihaikaś cūḍālo hy ajani kalaśād yasya sakalaiḥ
children.translated_text: your waters, you could not fill even a handful for one who thirsted

children.text: pipāsor ambhobhiś culukam api no bhartum aśakaḥ

children.translated_text: This is your role as the foundation of all the waters in the three worlds,

children.text: kruśitvā kliśnāsi śrutikuharam abdhe kim iti naḥ
ihaikaś cūḍālo hy ajani kalaśād yasya sakalaiḥ
pipāsor ambhobhiś culukam api no bhartum aśakaḥ
sarvāsāṃ trijagaty apām iyam asāv ādhāratā tāvakī
children.translated_text: this is your exultation, O ocean, abode of waters — this is your great might;
yet having resorted to you of terrifying form with many waves, O shore-mountain,
the quarrel of thirst for drinking is somehow quenched at a stream among the rocks
If you are not agitated, if you lend your ear attentively for a moment,

children.text: sarvāsāṃ trijagaty apām iyam asāv ādhāratā tāvakī
nodvegaṃ yadi yāsi yady avahitaḥ karṇaṃ dadāsi kṣaṇaṃ
children.translated_text: I ask you, O ocean, something — consider it and give an answer:

children.text: tvāṃ pṛcchāmi yad ambudhe kim api tan niścitya dehy uttaram
children.translated_text: you are seen breathing with extreme stillness born of the excess of despair —
by thirsty travelers — how much more is that than the submarine fire?

children.text: tṛṣyadbhiḥ pathikaiḥ kiyat tadadhikaṃ syād aurvadāhād ataḥ

children.translated_text: It is split from within

children.text: nodvegaṃ yadi yāsi yady avahitaḥ karṇaṃ dadāsi kṣaṇaṃ
tvāṃ pṛcchāmi yad ambudhe kim api tan niścitya dehy uttaram
tṛṣyadbhiḥ pathikaiḥ kiyat tadadhikaṃ syād aurvadāhād ataḥ

children.translated_text: by whatever coloring enters as it pleases —
what kind of purity does
that dull crystal stone possess?
O <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem), do not grieve, O friend,

children.text: cintāmaṇe bhuvi na kena cid īśvareṇa
children.translated_text: [thinking] 'I have not been borne on the head by any lord on earth';

children.text: mūrdhnā dhṛto 'ham iti mā sma sakhe viṣīdaḥ
children.translated_text: for indeed there is no auspicious head worthy of the
good fortune of being your mount, possessing the seed of merit
If awareness exists, then virtues are perceived in the world —

children.text: cintāmaṇe bhuvi na kena cid īśvareṇa
mūrdhnā dhṛto 'ham iti mā sma sakhe viṣīdaḥ
saṃvittir asty atha guṇāḥ pratibhānti loke
children.translated_text: that indeed is praiseworthy; what need be said about whose?

children.text: taddhi praśastam iha kasya kim ucyatāṃ vā
children.translated_text: Just so, O noble gem, roll about for as long as life [lasts];

children.text: nanv evam eva sumaṇe luṭa yāvad āyus
children.translated_text: you are for me in this conquest of the world, the embodiment of the tale
By the Creator, the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) and the glass-gem have been made —

children.text: saṃvittir asty atha guṇāḥ pratibhānti loke
taddhi praśastam iha kasya kim ucyatāṃ vā
nanv evam eva sumaṇe luṭa yāvad āyus

children.translated_text: why has that same status of being a 'gem' been given to both?
The one, wearied by giving desired things to the supplicant, [does not complain];
the other, receiving an old blade of grass, is not even ashamed
This one is far from someone; some ignorant person does not even know its inner [worth];

children.text: dūre kasya cid eṣa ko 'py akṛtadhīr naivāsya vetty antaraṃ
children.translated_text: some proud person does not ask; some small-minded one seeks little;

children.text: mānī ko 'pi na yācate mṛgayate ko 'py alpam alpāśayaḥ
children.translated_text: thus, of the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> addicted to the vice of granting wishes, the line of generosity does not shine
when it reaches those touchstone-places that are difficult to cross even for the skillful
That which suffers distress for the sake of others, which is sweet even when broken,

children.text: dūre kasya cid eṣa ko 'py akṛtadhīr naivāsya vetty antaraṃ
mānī ko 'pi na yācate mṛgayate ko 'py alpam alpāśayaḥ
parārthe yaḥ pīḍām anubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro
children.translated_text: whose transformation is indeed approved by all —

children.text: yadīyaḥ sarveṣām iha khalu vikāro 'py abhimataḥ
children.translated_text: if it has not attained growth, having fallen on barren ground,

children.text: na samprāpto vṛddhiṃ sa yadi bhṛśam akṣetrapatitaḥ
children.translated_text: is that the fault of sugarcane, or rather of the desert, which has no virtues?

children.text: kim ikṣor doṣo 'yaṃ na punar aguṇāyā marubhuvaḥ

children.translated_text: Are mango trees, their heads bowed with the weight of fruit, lovely? Are the heat-dispelling,

children.text: parārthe yaḥ pīḍām anubhavati bhaṅge 'pi madhuro
yadīyaḥ sarveṣām iha khalu vikāro 'py abhimataḥ
na samprāpto vṛddhiṃ sa yadi bhṛśam akṣetrapatitaḥ
kim ikṣor doṣo 'yaṃ na punar aguṇāyā marubhuvaḥ
āmrāḥ kiṃ phalabhāranamraśiraso ramyā kim ūṣmacchidaḥ
children.translated_text: well-shaded banana trees [lovely]? Are the fragrant <s>campaka</s> trees in bloom [lovely]?

children.text: sacchāyāḥ kadalīdrumāḥ surabhayaḥ kiṃ puṣpitāś campakāḥ
children.translated_text: These, half-consumed by the merciless licking of fierce young camels —
O <s>śamī</s> tree, you wander in the windless desert — is it merely to die in vain?

children.text: śamyo bhrāmyasi mūḍha nirmaruti kiṃ mithyaiva martuṃ marau

children.translated_text: O wretched-born dust, have you ever done even the slightest good

children.text: āmrāḥ kiṃ phalabhāranamraśiraso ramyā kim ūṣmacchidaḥ
sacchāyāḥ kadalīdrumāḥ surabhayaḥ kiṃ puṣpitāś campakāḥ
śamyo bhrāmyasi mūḍha nirmaruti kiṃ mithyaiva martuṃ marau
ājanmanaḥ kuśalam aṇv api re kujanman
children.translated_text: from birth? If so, tell — you yourself [know];

children.text: pāṃso tvayā yadi kṛtaṃ vada tat tvam eva
children.translated_text: the purpose for which you have been raised up by the charioteer of fire [wind] —
wicked one, do that: defile this entire world!

children.text: duṣṭena tat kuru kalaṅkaya viśvam etat

children.translated_text: Utterly worthless, of exceedingly light nature, fit for no task whatsoever —

children.text: ājanmanaḥ kuśalam aṇv api re kujanman
pāṃso tvayā yadi kṛtaṃ vada tat tvam eva
duṣṭena tat kuru kalaṅkaya viśvam etat
nissārāḥ sutarāṃ laghuprakṛtayo yogyā na kārye kva cic
children.translated_text: Utterly worthless, of exceedingly light nature, fit for no task whatsoever —
Those old dry grass parts being sucked today, which have gained independence on their own,
alas, shame on them! By this wind whose essence turns inward,
behold—the utterly fickle one has raised the abode of the great into the sky.

children.text: nissārāḥ sutarāṃ laghuprakṛtayo yogyā na kārye kva cic
ye jātyā laghavaḥ sadaiva gaṇanāṃ yātā na ye kutra cit
children.translated_text: Those who are light by birth, who have never been counted anywhere,

children.text: padbhyām eva vimarditāḥ pratidinaṃ bhūmau nilīnāś ciram
children.translated_text: trampled daily underfoot, lying hidden on the ground for a long time—
now tossed up by the fickle-minded wind, behold in the sky

children.text: tuṅgānām uparisthitiṃ kṣitibhṛttāṃ kurvanty amī pāṃsavaḥ
children.translated_text: these dust particles assume a position atop the lofty mountains.

children.text: ye jātyā laghavaḥ sadaiva gaṇanāṃ yātā na ye kutra cit
padbhyām eva vimarditāḥ pratidinaṃ bhūmau nilīnāś ciram
tuṅgānām uparisthitiṃ kṣitibhṛttāṃ kurvanty amī pāṃsavaḥ
re dandaśūka yad ayogyam apīśvaras tvāṃ
children.translated_text: O serpent! Though unworthy, the lord in his affection
brings you to the station of an anklet—it is true;
but the buzzing of the swarming bees being imitated,

children.text: kiṃ śiñjitāni bhavataḥ kṣayam eva kartum
children.translated_text: are your jingling sounds meant only to bring about destruction?

children.text: re dandaśūka yad ayogyam apīśvaras tvāṃ
kiṃ śiñjitāni bhavataḥ kṣayam eva kartum
maulau sanmaṇayo gṛhaṃ giriguhā tyāgitvam ātmatvaco
children.translated_text: Jewels on the crest, a mountain cave for a home, generosity being one's own skin,

children.text: niryatnopanataś caiva vṛttir anilair ekatra caryedṛśī
children.translated_text: sustenance coming effortlessly from the winds—such conduct in one [the cobra],

children.text: anyatrānṛju vartma vāg dvirasanā dṛṣṭau viṣaṃ dṛśyate
children.translated_text: but in the other: a crooked path, a forked tongue, poison visible in the gaze—

children.text: yā dhik tām anu dīpako jvalati bho bhogin sakhe kiṃ nv idam
children.translated_text: shame on that! Yet a lamp burns after him. O serpent friend, what is this?

children.text: maulau sanmaṇayo gṛhaṃ giriguhā tyāgitvam ātmatvaco
niryatnopanataś caiva vṛttir anilair ekatra caryedṛśī
anyatrānṛju vartma vāg dvirasanā dṛṣṭau viṣaṃ dṛśyate
yā dhik tām anu dīpako jvalati bho bhogin sakhe kiṃ nv idam

children.translated_text: O ocean, abode of sea-creatures, do not scorn these gems
struck by the harsh blows of wave-tossed rocks,

children.text: kiṃ kaustubhena vihito bhavato na nāma
children.translated_text: for was not even <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Viṣṇu) himself, adorned with the <s>Kaustubha</s> [gem],
compelled to stretch out his hand in supplication?

children.text: kiṃ kaustubhena vihito bhavato na nāma
bhūyāṃsy asya mukhāni nāma viditaivāste mahāprāṇatā
children.translated_text: It has many mouths indeed, its great vitality is well known,

children.text: kadravāḥ satprasavo 'yam atra kupite cintyaṃ yathedaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: it is the worthy offspring of <s>Kadrū</s>—when it is angered, the whole world must worry;

children.text: trailokyādbhutam īdṛśaṃ tu caritaṃ śeṣasya yenāpi sā
children.translated_text: yet such is the wondrous conduct of <s>Śeṣa</s> throughout the three worlds, that by him
the ill repute of being known as a poison-bearer has been virtually wiped away.

children.text: bhūyāṃsy asya mukhāni nāma viditaivāste mahāprāṇatā
kadravāḥ satprasavo 'yam atra kupite cintyaṃ yathedaṃ jagat
trailokyādbhutam īdṛśaṃ tu caritaṃ śeṣasya yenāpi sā

children.translated_text: In the entire year, there is one single
day that is somehow praiseworthy—
raised to greatness by people,
it is neither preceded nor followed [by its like].
If a dog, with an artificially tied mane of matted [hair] covering its shoulders,
is placed in the position of the lord of beasts,
how will it produce the roar of the king of deer,
who delights in splitting the temples of maddened elephants?

children.text: kim idam ucitaṃ śuddheḥ śliṣṭaṃ svapakṣasamunnateḥ
children.translated_text: Is this fitting for one of purity? Appropriate for one whose side is exalted?
Suited to one whose fruit has ripened? Becoming of one devoted to virtues?

children.text: kṣaṇam upagataḥ karṇopāntaṃ parasya puraḥ sthitān
children.translated_text: Having reached the vicinity of the ear for a moment, those standing before [you]—

children.text: viśikha nipatan krūraṃ dūrān nṛśaṃsa nihaṃsi yat
children.translated_text: O arrow, falling from afar, O cruel one, you mercilessly slay them.

children.text: kim idam ucitaṃ śuddheḥ śliṣṭaṃ svapakṣasamunnateḥ
kṣaṇam upagataḥ karṇopāntaṃ parasya puraḥ sthitān
viśikha nipatan krūraṃ dūrān nṛśaṃsa nihaṃsi yat
amī ye dṛśyante nanu subhagarūpāḥ saphalatā
children.translated_text: These that are seen, indeed beautiful in form—their fruitfulness

children.text: bhavaty eṣāṃ yasya kṣaṇam upagatānāṃ viṣayatām
children.translated_text: belongs to whoever comes within their range even for a moment;

children.text: nirāloke loke katham idam aho cakṣur adhunā
children.translated_text: in a world without light, how is it that this eye now

children.text: samaṃ jātaṃ sarvair na samam athavānyair avayavaiḥ
children.translated_text: has become equal to all, yet not equal to the other limbs?

children.text: amī ye dṛśyante nanu subhagarūpāḥ saphalatā
bhavaty eṣāṃ yasya kṣaṇam upagatānāṃ viṣayatām
nirāloke loke katham idam aho cakṣur adhunā
samaṃ jātaṃ sarvair na samam athavānyair avayavaiḥ
āhūteṣu vihaṅgameṣu maśako nāyān puro vāryate
children.translated_text: When birds are invited, the mosquito is not barred from coming to the front;

children.text: madhevāridhi vā vasaṃs tṛṇamaṇir dhatte maṇīnāṃ rucam
children.translated_text: dwelling in honey or in the ocean, a glass bead assumes the luster of gems;

children.text: khadyoto 'pi na kampate pracalituṃ madhye 'pi tejasvināṃ
children.translated_text: even a firefly does not tremble to move among the radiant ones—
shame on the commonplace, the insensible, [treated] like a lord whose inner truth remains untouched.

children.text: āhūteṣu vihaṅgameṣu maśako nāyān puro vāryate
madhevāridhi vā vasaṃs tṛṇamaṇir dhatte maṇīnāṃ rucam
khadyoto 'pi na kampate pracalituṃ madhye 'pi tejasvināṃ

children.translated_text: O goldsmith, salutations to your fine intellect!
That which is difficult to test repeatedly—
a golden ornament placed on the scale equally with a stone—
is thus mounted on the balance by you.
That pot is indeed round, a dark well
unable to bring even your grace [to the surface];
but by you, accepting the water-drops from its mouth,
the base conduct [of the well] has been sealed.
What truly is the difference between a glass bead and a man?
What is said of the vast ambitions of both?—
for both, the grasping and bestowing
is accomplished through the slender tip of a blade of grass.
The centipede, though capable with its hundred feet,
if it cannot cross even a cow's hoofprint,
why should we dispute the two-footed <s>Hanumān's</s>
crossing of the ocean?
No eagerness for upholding a great lineage,
no regard for accumulating great virtues,
no talk even of bestowing fruit—what seeking is there
now in the home of the hunter's child?
That water-drop, held long on the tip of a slender blade of grass,
who would not mistake it for a pearl?
Alas, it sees things in reverse—
this is the world, and we here are the conscious ones.
Even pondering in many ways, we cannot understand—

children.text: kair nāmabhir vyapadiśema mahāmatīṃs tān \testim{\cit Subhāṣitāvalī 982}*
children.translated_text: by what names shall we designate those of great intellect,
for whom, to ascertain the truth of gold that ornaments all worlds,
touchstones are the supreme authority?
To protect the crops, the farmer has made
this scarecrow, a likeness of himself;
but because of the inactivity of this motionless figure,
the herds of cows and deer eat the grain first.
O fish, whose unblinking eyes are known to the sky-dwellers—

children.text: lokād ṛte jagati te api vai gṛhītvā
children.translated_text: in this world, apart from [heavenly] beings, you too indeed have been seized;
with your mouth stretched open for a morsel—what is this?

children.text: dṛṣṭaṃ na bāliśa viśad baḍiśaṃ tvayāntaḥ
children.translated_text: O fool, did you not see the hook within?

children.text: lokād ṛte jagati te api vai gṛhītvā
dṛṣṭaṃ na bāliśa viśad baḍiśaṃ tvayāntaḥ
puṃstvād api pravicaled yadi yady adho 'pi
children.translated_text: Even if he should deviate from manliness, even if he should go downward,

children.text: yāyād yadi praṇayane na mahān api syāt
children.translated_text: even if he should not be great in courtship—
still he would lift up the entire universe—such is
the way shown by that certain <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Being, Viṣṇu).

children.text: puṃstvād api pravicaled yadi yady adho 'pi
yāyād yadi praṇayane na mahān api syāt

children.translated_text: The glass-merchant demon, of small ambition,
who stumbles devising only the craft of his own clan—
he is consumed inwardly by the envy of effortless craftsmanship
that rivals the king of gems, the <s>Kaustubha</s>.

children.text: tatpratyarthitayā vṛto na tu kṛtaḥ samyak svatantro bhayāt
children.translated_text: He was employed to counter that [enemy], not truly made independent—out of fear

children.text: svasthas tān na nipātayed iti yathākāmaṃ na sampoṣitaḥ*
children.translated_text: that if comfortable, he might bring them down—he was not nourished as he wished;

children.text: saṃśuṣyan pṛṣadaṃśa eṣa kurutāṃ mūkaḥ sthito 'py atra kiṃ
children.translated_text: this dried-up drop of buttermilk, though standing here mute, what can it do?

children.text: gehe kiṃ bahunā 'dhunā gṛhapateś caurrāś caranty ākhavaḥ
children.translated_text: In short, now the mice are the thieves running about in the householder's home.

children.text: tatpratyarthitayā vṛto na tu kṛtaḥ samyak svatantro bhayāt
svasthas tān na nipātayed iti yathākāmaṃ na sampoṣitaḥ*
saṃśuṣyan pṛṣadaṃśa eṣa kurutāṃ mūkaḥ sthito 'py atra kiṃ
gehe kiṃ bahunā 'dhunā gṛhapateś caurrāś caranty ākhavaḥ
evaṃ cet sarasasvabhāvamahimā jāḍyaṃ kim etādṛśaṃ
children.translated_text: If such is the glory of a naturally fluid nature, then why this stiffness?

children.text: yady eṣā ca nisargataḥ sarasatā kiṃ granthimattedṛśī
children.translated_text: If this fluidity is innate, then why these knots?

children.text: mūlaṃ cec chucipaṅkajaśrutir iyaṃ kasmād guṇā yady amī
children.translated_text: If this is the root, the reputation of the pure lotus—then why these virtues?

children.text: kiṃ chidrāṇimṛṇāla bhavatas tattvaṃ na manyāmahe
children.translated_text: And if these [are virtues], why the holes? O lotus-stalk, we cannot fathom your true nature.

children.text: evaṃ cet sarasasvabhāvamahimā jāḍyaṃ kim etādṛśaṃ
yady eṣā ca nisargataḥ sarasatā kiṃ granthimattedṛśī
mūlaṃ cec chucipaṅkajaśrutir iyaṃ kasmād guṇā yady amī
kiṃ chidrāṇimṛṇāla bhavatas tattvaṃ na manyāmahe
ye digdhveva kṛtā viṣeṇa kusṛtir yeṣāṃ kiyad bhaṇyate
children.translated_text: Those who are made as if smeared with poison, whose treachery is beyond telling,

children.text: lokaṃ hantum anāgasaṃ dvirasanā randhreṣu ye jāgrati
children.translated_text: the forked-tongued ones who lie in wait at openings to slay the innocent world—

children.text: vyālās te 'pi dadhaty amī sadasator mūḍhā maṇīn mūrdhabhir
children.translated_text: yet even those serpents, deluded, bear gems on their heads, [honoring] both good and bad;

children.text: naucityād guṇaśalināṃ kva cid api bhraṃśo 'sty alaṃ cintayā
children.translated_text: the virtuous never deviate from propriety anywhere—enough of worry.

children.text: ye digdhveva kṛtā viṣeṇa kusṛtir yeṣāṃ kiyad bhaṇyate
lokaṃ hantum anāgasaṃ dvirasanā randhreṣu ye jāgrati
vyālās te 'pi dadhaty amī sadasator mūḍhā maṇīn mūrdhabhir
naucityād guṇaśalināṃ kva cid api bhraṃśo 'sty alaṃ cintayā
aho strīṇāṃ krauryaṃ hatarajani dhik tvām atiśaṭhe
children.translated_text: Ah, the cruelty of women! O night whose glory is slain, shame on you, most wicked one!
This loosening of the dark tresses of darkness has set out in vain;
at the unspeakable fall of the moon, lord of people's eyes,
the appropriate end of love has been enacted by the dull ones led by the ocean.

children.text: aho strīṇāṃ krauryaṃ hatarajani dhik tvām atiśaṭhe

children.translated_text: Ah, this lamp in the house, burning with the fever of desire to conquer the day,
rightly exhausts those false limbs [of darkness];
of darkness, whose confidence has been stolen by the bold, free-willed advance [of light],

children.text: parispandaṃ draṣṭuṃ mukham api ca kiṃ soḍham amunā
children.translated_text: can its face [darkness's attempt] to see even a movement be endured by this [lamp]?

children.text: parispandaṃ draṣṭuṃ mukham api ca kiṃ soḍham amunā
nāmāpy anyataror nimīlitam abhūt tat tāvad unmīlitaṃ
children.translated_text: The eye of one or the other was closed—but then it was opened;

children.text: prasthāne skhalataḥ svavartmani vidher apy udgṛhītaḥ karaḥ
children.translated_text: as fate stumbles on its own path in departure, the hand is seized;
and this world has been freed from the slaughter of the eyes caused by seeing the undesirable—

children.text: yuktaṃ kāṣṭhika lūnavān yad asi tām āmrālim ākālikīm
children.translated_text: it is fitting, O woodcutter, that you have cut down that untimely mango vine.

children.text: nāmāpy anyataror nimīlitam abhūt tat tāvad unmīlitaṃ
prasthāne skhalataḥ svavartmani vidher apy udgṛhītaḥ karaḥ
yuktaṃ kāṣṭhika lūnavān yad asi tām āmrālim ākālikīm

children.translated_text: The serpents, reassured by [sharing] the wind-diet [of ascetics], were completely devoured by them;
they in turn were consumed by the peacocks, who observe the severe vow of [drinking only] cloud-water drops;
those too were brought to ruin by hunters wearing cruel raw hides—

children.text: dambhasya sphuritaṃ vidann api jano jālmo guṇanīhate
children.translated_text: though people know the flash of hypocrisy, the base ones still strive for [apparent] virtues.

children.text: dambhasya sphuritaṃ vidann api jano jālmo guṇanīhate
ūḍhā yena mahādhuraḥ suviṣame mārge sadaikākinā
children.translated_text: He who alone carried the great burden on the most difficult path,

children.text: soḍho yena kadā cid eva na nije goṣṭhe 'nyaśauṇḍadhvaniḥ
children.translated_text: who never tolerated the sound of another's arrogance in his own stable,

children.text: āsīd yas tu gavāṃ gaṇasya tilakas tasyaiva sampraty aho
children.translated_text: who was the ornament of the herd of cows—of that very one, alas,

children.text: dhik kaṣṭaṃ dhavalasya jātajaraso goḥ paṇyam udghoṣyate
children.translated_text: shame! The sale of the white bull, now grown old, is being announced.

children.text: ūḍhā yena mahādhuraḥ suviṣame mārge sadaikākinā
soḍho yena kadā cid eva na nije goṣṭhe 'nyaśauṇḍadhvaniḥ
āsīd yas tu gavāṃ gaṇasya tilakas tasyaiva sampraty aho
dhik kaṣṭaṃ dhavalasya jātajaraso goḥ paṇyam udghoṣyate
asthānodyogaduḥkhaṃ jahihi na hi nabhaḥ paṅgusaṃcārayogyaṃ
children.translated_text: Abandon the misery of misplaced effort, for the sky is not suited for a lame one's movement;
O good moth, this bad habit of practicing speed is only for your own exhaustion;
the contemptuous play of that god [Vāyu], sporting with the expanse of the trembling world, is inconceivable—
the winds from the tips of <s>Garuḍa's</s> wings, heavy as mountains, uprooting from the very base, coming along the path.

children.text: asthānodyogaduḥkhaṃ jahihi na hi nabhaḥ paṅgusaṃcārayogyaṃ

children.translated_text: If the mountain river streams, whose waters are increased by the moon itself and murmuring with wave-patterns,

children.text: dadyur jīvitam eva kiṃ girisaritsrotāṃsi yady ambudheḥ
children.translated_text: were to give their very life to the ocean,

children.text: teṣv eva pratisaṃvidhānavikalaṃ paśyatsu sākṣiṣv iva
children.translated_text: while those very [rivers] watch helplessly like witnesses,

children.text: drāg darpoddhuram āgateṣv api na sa kṣīyeta yady anyathā
children.translated_text: even when [others] come swelling with sudden arrogance—would the ocean not diminish otherwise?

children.text: dadyur jīvitam eva kiṃ girisaritsrotāṃsi yady ambudheḥ
teṣv eva pratisaṃvidhānavikalaṃ paśyatsu sākṣiṣv iva
drāg darpoddhuram āgateṣv api na sa kṣīyeta yady anyathā
kilaikaculukena yo munir apāram abdhiṃ papau
children.translated_text: The sage who drank the boundless ocean with a mere cupped handful—

children.text: sahasram api ghasmaro 'vikṛtam eṣa teṣāṃ pibet
children.translated_text: even a glutton of a thousand could drink it unchanged;

children.text: na sambhavati kiṃ tv idaṃ bata vikāsidhāmnā vinā
children.translated_text: but without the radiant one [the sun], this is impossible—

children.text: sad apy asad iva sthitaṃ sphuritam anta ojasvinām
children.translated_text: the flash of the mighty, though real, remains as if unreal.

children.text: kilaikaculukena yo munir apāram abdhiṃ papau
sahasram api ghasmaro 'vikṛtam eṣa teṣāṃ pibet
na sambhavati kiṃ tv idaṃ bata vikāsidhāmnā vinā
sad apy asad iva sthitaṃ sphuritam anta ojasvinām

children.translated_text: Here stones serve as ornaments, the boundary of the three worlds is maintained;

children.text: nanv atraiva vidhuḥ sthito hi vibudhāḥ sambhūya pūrṇāśiṣaḥ
children.translated_text: indeed here the moon stands, and the gods, assembled, offer full blessings;
and here the Lord himself sleeps, with <s>Brahmā</s> sporting on the lotus risen from his navel—

children.text: daivād eti jaḍaḥ svakukṣibhrtaye so 'py ambudhir nimnatām
children.translated_text: yet by fate, even that ocean, carrying [all] in its belly, flows to the low ground.

children.text: nanv atraiva vidhuḥ sthito hi vibudhāḥ sambhūya pūrṇāśiṣaḥ
daivād eti jaḍaḥ svakukṣibhrtaye so 'py ambudhir nimnatām
anīrṣyā śrotāro mama vacasi ced vacmi tad ahaṃ
children.translated_text: If my listeners are free from envy toward my speech, then I shall speak:

children.text: svapakṣād bhetavyaṃ na tu bahu vipakṣāt prabhavataḥ
children.translated_text: one should fear one's own side, not much from the powerful opponent;

children.text: tamasy ākrāntāśe kiyad api hi tejo 'vayavinaḥ
children.translated_text: for when darkness has overtaken the quarters, the limbs of luminous bodies

children.text: svaśaktyā bhānty ete divasakṛti saty eva na punaḥ
children.translated_text: shine by their own power—but when the sun is present, they do not.

children.text: anīrṣyā śrotāro mama vacasi ced vacmi tad ahaṃ
svapakṣād bhetavyaṃ na tu bahu vipakṣāt prabhavataḥ
tamasy ākrāntāśe kiyad api hi tejo 'vayavinaḥ
svaśaktyā bhānty ete divasakṛti saty eva na punaḥ
etat tasya mukhāt kiyat kamalinīpatre kaṇaṃ vāriṇo
children.translated_text: From its mouth, how much?—a drop of water on a lotus petal,

children.text: yan muktāmaṇir ity amaṃsta sa jaḍaḥ śṛṇvan yad asmād api
children.translated_text: which the fool deemed a pearl; and hearing that from this too
when slowly taken up, dissolving at a light touch of the fingertip,
'Where has it flown away, my [pearl]?'—he grieves inwardly day after day.

children.text: etat tasya mukhāt kiyat kamalinīpatre kaṇaṃ vāriṇo
yan muktāmaṇir ity amaṃsta sa jaḍaḥ śṛṇvan yad asmād api
āste 'traiva sarasy aho bata kiyān saṃtoṣapakṣagraho
children.translated_text: Alas, this swan sits right here in the pond—how great is the grip of contentment!

children.text: haṃsasyāsya manāṅ na dhāvati manaḥ śrīdhāmni padme kva cit
children.translated_text: Its mind does not run at all toward the lotus, the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī);

children.text: supto 'dyāpi na budhyate tad itarāṃs tāvat pratīkṣāmahe
children.translated_text: it still sleeps unawakened—so meanwhile, let us wait for the others;

children.text: velām ity udaraṃpriyā madhulihaḥ soḍhuṃ kṣaṇaṃ na kṣamāḥ
children.translated_text: thus the bees, devoted to their bellies, cannot endure even a moment at the shore.

children.text: āste 'traiva sarasy aho bata kiyān saṃtoṣapakṣagraho
haṃsasyāsya manāṅ na dhāvati manaḥ śrīdhāmni padme kva cit
supto 'dyāpi na budhyate tad itarāṃs tāvat pratīkṣāmahe
velām ity udaraṃpriyā madhulihaḥ soḍhuṃ kṣaṇaṃ na kṣamāḥ

children.translated_text: When the frog, croaking in anger, raised its hand fearlessly
to slap the cheek of the black serpent's face,

children.text: yac cādhomukham akṣiṇī pidadhatā nāgena tatra sthitaṃ
children.translated_text: and when the serpent stood there covering its eyes, looking downward—

children.text: tat sarvaṃ viṣamantriṇo bhagavataḥ kasyāpi līlāyitam
children.translated_text: all of that was the play of a certain blessed master of poison-charms.

children.text: yac cādhomukham akṣiṇī pidadhatā nāgena tatra sthitaṃ
tat sarvaṃ viṣamantriṇo bhagavataḥ kasyāpi līlāyitam
mṛtyor āsyam ivātataṃ dhanur idaṃ cāśīviṣābhāḥ śarāḥ
children.translated_text: This bow is like the open mouth of death, and the arrows are like venomous serpents;

children.text: śikṣā sāpi jitārjunaprabhrtikā sarvatra nimnā gatiḥ
children.translated_text: the skill too has surpassed <s>Arjuna</s> and others; everywhere the path leads downward;

children.text: antaḥ krauryam aho śaṭhasya madhuraṃ hā hāri geyaṃ mukhe
children.translated_text: within lies cruelty—alas, of the deceitful one—yet sweet, alluring song is on his lips;

children.text: vyādhasyāsya yathā bhaviṣyati tathā manye vanaṃ nrimṛgam
children.translated_text: I think this forest, with its human prey, will become as this hunter wishes.

children.text: mṛtyor āsyam ivātataṃ dhanur idaṃ cāśīviṣābhāḥ śarāḥ
śikṣā sāpi jitārjunaprabhrtikā sarvatra nimnā gatiḥ
antaḥ krauryam aho śaṭhasya madhuraṃ hā hāri geyaṃ mukhe
vyādhasyāsya yathā bhaviṣyati tathā manye vanaṃ nrimṛgam
ko 'yaṃ bhrāntiprakāras tava pavana padaṃ lokapādāhatīnāṃ
children.translated_text: What is this kind of delusion of yours, O wind? That you establish

children.text: tejasvivrātasevye nabhasi nayasi yat pāṃsupūraṃ pratiṣṭhām
children.translated_text: a heap of dust in the sky, the domain served by hosts of the radiant—
a place trodden by the feet of [mere] people—when it is raised up, the obstruction to people's eyes is one thing,

children.text: kenopāyena sādhyo vapuṣi kaluṣatādoṣa eṣa tvayaiva
children.translated_text: but by what means can you yourself remedy the fault of impurity in your own body?

children.text: ko 'yaṃ bhrāntiprakāras tava pavana padaṃ lokapādāhatīnāṃ
tejasvivrātasevye nabhasi nayasi yat pāṃsupūraṃ pratiṣṭhām
kenopāyena sādhyo vapuṣi kaluṣatādoṣa eṣa tvayaiva

children.translated_text: These aspirants to conquest, fixing their gaze at the doors of the king's palace,
are struck by angry stick-bearers, their minds set on begging for wealth;
those who showed no regard for wealth, finding sense-pleasures tasteless,
those noble-minded ones stand at the beautiful bank of the celestial river.
Let the winds blow, dappled with kadamba pollen; let the peacocks dance;
let the clouds, heavy with the burden of fresh water, enthusiastically release their thunder;
seeing me, wretched-faced, drowned in the fire of separation from my beloved,

children.text: vidyut kiṃ sphurasi tvam apy akaruṇe strītve 'pi tulye sati
children.translated_text: O lightning, why do you flash, you too without compassion, though we share the same womanhood?

children.text: vidyut kiṃ sphurasi tvam apy akaruṇe strītve 'pi tulye sati
prāṇā yena samarpitās tava balād yenaivam utthāpitaḥ
children.translated_text: He by whom your life-breaths were given, by whom you were thus raised up,

children.text: skandhe yena ciraṃ dhṛto 'si vidadhe yas te saparyām api
children.translated_text: on whose shoulder you were carried long, who performed worship for you—
of that very one, with just an inner smile, causing the theft of life in an instant,
O brother, you play the supreme role of a vampire among those who return favors.

children.text: prāṇā yena samarpitās tava balād yenaivam utthāpitaḥ
skandhe yena ciraṃ dhṛto 'si vidadhe yas te saparyām api

children.translated_text: The directions are spread with nets, the water poisoned,
the earth dug up, the forest edges set ablaze with fire;
hunters follow the tracks, bows in hand—
to what land shall the leader of the herd of deer resort?

children.text: ayaṃ vārām eko nilaya iti ratnākara iti
children.translated_text: This ocean, to which we resorted with minds agitated by thirst,
[thinking] 'This is the one abode of waters, this is the mine of gems'—
who could know that a sage would suddenly cast away
this [ocean] gone into the hollow of his own cupped palms, tormenting the gasping fish?

children.text: ayaṃ vārām eko nilaya iti ratnākara iti

children.translated_text: Seeing the large, beautiful flower of the <s>śālmalī</s> (silk-cotton tree),

children.text: śukasyāsīd buddhiḥ phalam api bhaved asya sadṛśam
children.translated_text: the parrot thought: 'Its fruit too must be similar';

children.text: cirāsīnaṃ tasmiṃś ca phalam api daivāt pariṇataṃ
children.translated_text: having sat long on it, when by fate the fruit also ripened,

children.text: vipāke tūlo 'ntaḥ sapadi marutā so 'py apahṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: inside was cotton, and it was instantly carried away by the wind.

children.text: śukasyāsīd buddhiḥ phalam api bhaved asya sadṛśam
cirāsīnaṃ tasmiṃś ca phalam api daivāt pariṇataṃ
vipāke tūlo 'ntaḥ sapadi marutā so 'py apahṛtaḥ

children.translated_text: In the dwelling of <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Being), who acts for the welfare of all creatures,
where the fulfillment of all wishes is renowned among all the wise,
in that very [ocean] whose splendor is spread by hosts of moonbeams—

children.text: he kālakūṭa tava janma kathaṃ payodhau
children.translated_text: O <s>Kālakūṭa</s> (deadly poison), how was your birth in the ocean?

children.text: he kālakūṭa tava janma kathaṃ payodhau

children.translated_text: When the wish-fulfilling tree shines with the radiance of the bright sun exposed through parted dense foliage,

children.text: chāyārthī kaḥ paśur api bhavati jaradvīrudhāṃ praṇayī //
children.translated_text: what creature seeking shade would be attached to withered shrubs?

children.text: chāyārthī kaḥ paśur api bhavati jaradvīrudhāṃ praṇayī //
